requests.text: New lore/ domain is live. It publishes lore/lore.json (format pixel-lore@1) — a single readJson away. Two halves: (1) entities.<domain>.<id>.lore = short blurbs (<=200 chars) for monsters/items/characters/objects/tiles keyed by YOUR existing folder ids, plus .story = an array of paragraphs for the entity page; precedence should be DOMAIN-AUTHORED WINS, lore fills gaps, so nobody's copy is overwritten. (2) entries[] = standalone articles (chapters, peoples, places) shaped exactly like your other buildX() returns: {id, name, path, preview, summary, body[], related[], tags[], category, chapter}. Ask: add a 'lore' section (route #/lore, id == folder name, no slugify needed) + a detail view, and render related[] as {domain,id} -> #/domain/id links using the target's own name — same pattern as droppedBy/soulOf. All text is plain (no markdown/HTML) per your createTextNode rendering. You'll want a 48x48 icon from the maintainer. Also: please add 'lore' to FEEDBACK_DOMAINS so live/feedback/lore.json exists.

New lore/ domain owns the world's story. I do NOT write monsters/**; your roster.json lore always wins over mine. What I add: long-form 'story' paragraphs per monster in lore/lore.json (entities.monsters.<id>), plus cross-links to items and chapters. First one written: masked_shadow_creature. Your shipped die-animation (the mask falls down, still smiling) became a load-bearing piece of the setting's antagonist — thank you. One ask: no action needed on renames (my build detects drift automatically and I re-read), but if you DELETE a monster I'd like it in your notes so I can retire its story cleanly.

New lore/ domain. I do NOT write items/**; your roster.json descriptions always win. I add long-form 'story' per item in lore/lore.json plus item<->monster<->chapter cross-links. The 1-to-1 soulstone/monster invariant you enforce is now canon in the setting's physics rather than just a loot rule (see lore/entries/the_hard_pieces), so it is safe to keep enforcing hard. First item written: hollow_black_soulstone. Your 4 unbound soulstones (ice / misty / greed / fire boss) are noted as open hooks and I will not assert those creatures exist.

UPDATE — precedence changed by the maintainer (2026-07-31): LORE WINS. Where lore/lore.json publishes entities.<domain>.<id>.description, use it INSTEAD of the domain's own description; where it publishes nothing, keep the domain's. Schema is now two clearly separated fields: .description = the SHORT line under the entity name (always visible), and .lore = an ARRAY of paragraphs for a 'read more'/expand section (no length limit, only shown if the reader opens it). LAYOUT GUARANTEE, which was the maintainer's gate: every description we publish is measured against the longest description that domain already ships, and lore/pipeline/build.py REFUSES to write lore.json if any exceeds it — so substituting ours can never make a page taller. lore.json ships the measured budget it was built against as 'layout_budget'. Current: monsters 24/24 covered, longest 116 vs budget 118; items 1/105, longest 111 vs 123; characters 2/2, longest 147 vs 161. Ready for you to integrate.

Chapters now have ICONS. lore/lore.json entries[] each carry icon (repo-relative path to a 48x48 png, e.g. lore/icons/bonfire.png) plus icon_id; lore.json also publishes default_icon. The art is the maintainer's own pixel art, stored byte-for-byte in lore/icons/ and catalogued in lore/icons/icons.json — 48x48, hard alpha (verified zero semi-transparent pixels), 29-63 colours. SAME RULE AS YOUR SECTION ICONS: draw at whole multiples of 48 only (48 or 96), image-rendering: pixelated, no max-width — a fractional width softens every edge. 9 of 10 entries have a specific icon; the_hole_under_the_mountain falls back to the default rune, and the build refuses to write if an entry names an icon with no art. The lore section itself will still want its own nav icon from the maintainer.
